myths-and-legends-of-our-own-land-volume: The heartland takes center stage here, with legends from the central states and the Great Lakes — French voyageurs, frontier ghosts, and the spirits of the inland seas. Skinner's collection reminds us that the Midwest has folklore as rich as any coast. Sturdy, surprising stories from America's middle ground.
godliness-being-reports-of-a-series-of-a: Catherine Booth — the Mother of the Salvation Army — delivered these powerful addresses on holy living to crowded London halls. Taken down as she spoke, they carry her urgent, practical faith: godliness as a daily, lived reality. The reports preserve the voice of one of the nineteenth century's most remarkable women preachers.
st-patrick-s-day-or-the-scheming-lieuten: Richard Brinsley Sheridan — the great wit behind The School for Scandal — offers this brisk one-act farce of soldiers, sweethearts, and scheming. Written for a St. Patrick's Day benefit, it delivers mistaken identities and happy endings at top speed. A small, sparkling gem from the golden age of English comedy.
chimes-of-mission-bells-an-historical-sk: Maria Antonia Field sketches the history of California's missions — their founding by Franciscan padres, their Indigenous converts, and their romantic ruins. Written with affection for the Spanish past, the book preserves the lore of old California. A gentle, nostalgic history of the mission era.
fiat-money-inflation-in-france-how-it-ca: Andrew Dickson White — founder of Cornell University — traces France's disastrous experiment with paper money during the Revolution. His sober history of the assignats became the classic warning against inflation and easy money. Economics as tragedy, and a book every student of money should read.
